The induction effect of lumacaftor on CYP3A ensures that the net exposure of ivacaftor at steady-state does not exceed the exposure observed when ivacaftor is administered alone at its approved dose of 150 mg every 12 hours. Therefore, no dose adjustment is required when CYP3A inhibitors are initiated in patients already taking lumacaftor/ivacaftor. However, when starting lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients on strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose to one tablet daily (lumacaftor 200 mg/ivacaftor 125 mg total daily dose) for the first week to allow for the steady-state induction effect of lumacaftor. After this period, resume the recommended daily dose. No dose adjustment is needed for moderate or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 2. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Reduce the lumateperone dose to 21 mg/day if co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 3. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of lumefantrine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Maprotiline and isoniazid both increase serotonin levels. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 5. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Decrease the maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 6. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Initiation of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may require a decreased mavacamten dose. 7. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Monitor for adverse effects of mavorixafor if co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Reduce the mavorixafor daily dose if necessary. 8. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Isoniazid and meperidine both increase serotonin levels. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 11. Isoniazid decreases the effects of metformin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Patients should be observed for loss of blood glucose control. If drugs are withdrawn from a patient receiving metformin, monitor closely for hypoglycemia. 12. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of methadone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of isoniazid by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2E1 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of midazolam by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Milnacipran and isoniazid both increase serotonin levels. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 17. Mipomersen and isoniazid may increase the toxicity of each other. Use caution and monitor closely. Both drugs have the potential to increase hepatic enzymes; monitor liver function tests (LFTs). 18. Isoniazid and mirtazapine both increase serotonin levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Isoniazid and morphine both increase serotonin levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Isoniazid increases the levels of naldemedine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for potential adverse effects of naldemedine if co-administered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 21. Naratriptan and isoniazid both increase serotonin levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Nefazodone and isoniazid both increase serotonin levels. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 23. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Netupitant is mainly metabolized by CYP3A4; no dosage adjustment is required. 25. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of nifedipine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of nimodipine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of nitrendipine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of norgestrel by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentration of norgestrel, increasing the risk of adverse effects. 30. Nortriptyline and isoniazid both increase serotonin levels. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 31. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and titrate subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 32. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP450 inhibitors may decrease clearance of ondansetron; however, no dosage adjustment is recommended. 33. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of osilodrostat by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Reduce the dose of osilodrostat, a CYP3A4 substrate, by half when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 34. Isoniazid increases the levels of ospemifene by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel protein-bound by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Avoid co-administration of palovarotene, a CYP3A substrate, with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palovarotene dose by 50%. 38. Isoniazid increases the levels of panobinostat by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Reduce the panobinostat starting dose to 10 mg if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 39. Paroxetine and isoniazid both increase serotonin levels. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 40. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of pazopanib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid co-administration of pazopanib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors if possible; if co-administration is necessary, decrease the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. 41. Isoniazid and pentazocine both increase serotonin levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of pimozide by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of polatuzumab vedotin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a CYP3A4 substrate. Co-administration of polatuzumab vedotin with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor may increase unconjugated MMAE AUC, potentially increasing polatuzumab vedotin toxicities. 44. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of prednisolone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of prednisone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of propafenone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Protriptyline and isoniazid both increase serotonin levels. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 48. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of quetiapine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of quinidine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Rasagiline and isoniazid both increase serotonin levels. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 52. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of repaglinide by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Isoniazid increases the levels of rilpivirine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of ripretinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with a strong CYP3A inhibitor will increase systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), which may increase the risk of adverse reactions. 55. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Rizatriptan and isoniazid both increase serotonin levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Isoniazid and safinamide may increase the toxicity of each other by increasing serotonin levels. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Monitor for hypertension and reaction to dietary tyramine in patients treated concomitantly with isoniazid and safinamide. 59. Isoniazid and SAMe both increase serotonin levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of saxagliptin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Limit saxagliptin to 5 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 61. Isoniazid increases the levels of seladelpar by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Exercise caution in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers taking seladelpar and co-administered a moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 62. Selegiline and isoniazid both increase serotonin levels. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 63. Selegiline transdermal and isoniazid both increase serotonin levels. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 64. Sertraline and isoniazid both increase serotonin levels. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 65. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of sevoflurane by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2E1 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 66. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of sildenafil by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 67. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of isoniazid by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours. 68. Sodium citrate/citric acid decreases the levels of isoniazid by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours. 69. Isoniazid decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with antibiotics decreases efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. 70. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases the toxicity of isoniazid. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with medications that cause fluid and electrolyte abnormalities may increase the risk of adverse events such as seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. 71. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate increases the toxicity of isoniazid. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with medications that cause fluid and electrolyte abnormalities may increase the risk of adverse events such as seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. 72. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 73. Isoniazid and St. John’s Wort both increase serotonin levels. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 74. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of sufentanil by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 75. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of sufentanil SL by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of sufentanil SL with any CYP3A4 inhibitor may increase sufentanil plasma concentration, thereby increasing or prolonging adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. 76. Sumatriptan and isoniazid both increase serotonin levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 77. Sumatriptan intranasal and isoniazid both increase serotonin levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 78. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of sunitinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 79. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 80. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of tadalafil by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Limit tadalafil to 5 mg/day (for daily use) or 10 mg every 72 hours (for as-needed use). Avoid concurrent use of tadalafil for pulmonary hypertension in patients taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 81. Isoniazid and tamoxifen interact by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored.
